source_rows.r.content: RAN2 understand that multiple instances of PRS assistance data can already be supported by the current LPP spec. One or more NR-DL-PRS-AssistanceData-r16 elements can be provided in one or more LPP Assistance Data messages.

Proposal 4: UE may explicitly request on-demand PRS parameters based on the Rel-16 value ranges. [14/14]
Proposal 6: A UE reason/cause for an on-demand PRS request is not supported. [12/14]
Proposal 7: The posSI message cannot be the response for a UE’s On-Demand PRS request. [13/14]
Proposal 12: The DL-PRS-Configuration ID is only defined by an identifier (ID). [13/14]
Proposal 13: On-demand PRS configuration is at least provided per positioning method. [12/14]

Proposal 1 (modified): The SRS-TEG association reporting, if any, shall always be reported along with the UE Rx – Tx time difference measurement report for Multi-RTT with no additional periodicities (8/11) and to agree the TP on report of association for Multi-RTT in the annex (11/12). Any additional parameters can be discussed in the running CRs pending RAN1 input.
Proposal 2 (modified): For UL-TDOA, configure UE TxTEG Report Config in SRS-Config IE and a new RRC message to report the changes of UE TxTEG (9/11).
Proposal 5 (modified): Each of association information of UL SRS resources with timestamp indicating the change of the Tx TEG association (8/12) and agree the TP of UE-TxTEG-Report-v17xy-IEs via RRC in the annex.
Broadcast of TRP Tx TEG info and Measurement report
Proposal 6: RAN2 to agree new posSibType6-5  NR-DL-PRS-TRP-TEG-Info for the TRP Tx TEG info (10/11) and the TP of NR-DL-PRS-TRP-TEG-Info for broadcast(8/11) in the annex, FFS the description on resource association.
Proposal 8: RAN2 to agree the stage-3 design of RSTD measurements from different DL PRS resources per UE Rx TEG report in the annex (10/12).
Proposal 9: RAN2 to agree the updated stage-3 design of UE Rx-Tx time difference measurements obtained from different DL PRS resources per UE Rx TEG/ RxTx TEG in the annex (9/9), FFS the nr-UE-Tx-TEG-ID-r17 in case2 and case3.

Proposal 6: TA timer configuration of SRS for positioning (SRSp) is invalidated upon any cell reselection (i.e. even if the UE does not initiate the RRC resume procedure) (11/12)
Proposal 7: Follow CG-SDT solution for (a) RSRP derivation for positioning SRS TA validation, and (b) definition of stored downlink pathloss reference RSRP value at the very first positioning SRS transmission (12/12)

Granularity of response time:
Proposal point 3.2.1-1: [for agreements]  [6/9] 10ms Finer granularity is only applied for NR RAT dependent positioning methods;
Capabilities for integrity:
Proposal point 3.2.2-1: [for agreements]  [10/10] For GNSS integrity capability, adapt capabilities captured in the running LPP CR R2-2201723 as baseline;
TPs for individual capability items:
Proposal point 3.3.1-1: [for agreements]  [8/8] 27-1 TEG is captured as
[TPs in R2-2202494]

Proposal1: Scheduled location time is an absolute time in LPP spec. (14/15)
Proposal3: The indication of scheduled location time can be based on different time bases. (8/12)
Proposal5: No need to report area ID along with PRS measurement to the LMF if the PRS AD is associated with area ID. (9/10)
Proposal6 (modified): areaID can be broadcasted in the system information.  This has no spec impact if the area ID is defined to be something already broadcasted in the system information.  Detailed signalling can be further discussed in the LPP running CR discussion and in the context of defining the area ID.
Proposal10: eLCID is adopted for UL MAC CE for MG activation/deactivation request and DL MAC CE for MG activation/deactivation command. (13/13)
Proposal14: eLCID is adopted for DL MAC CE for PPW activation/deactivation command. (13/13)
Proposal15: Adopt the 10 milliseconds granularity in the responseTime. (13/13)

Proposal 1. For the purpose of GNSS integrity feature added in Release17, use GNSS-RealTimeIntegrity IE to signal to UE bad satellites (and GNSS constellations).
Proposal 2. Update description of GNSS-RealTimeIntegrity IE and Stage 2 to clarly state what condition can be interpreted as DNU = FALSE.

Proposal 1. Covariance parameters for Orbital errors are not included in Rel17. These terms, together with the full cross-covariance matrix, can be revisted in future releases and possibly coordinated with RTCM.

Proposal 2: Agree on Low Power Periodic and Triggered 5GC-MT-LR Procedure with SDT (in R2-2203443) for UL-only and UL+DL positioning in RRC_INACTIVE as baseline for Stage 2 discussion
Proposal 1: Add clarification note (as below) in Stage 2 specification:

Proposal 3 (modified):	A pre-defined on-demand DL-PRS configuration can be described with the Rel-16 IEs NR-DL-PRS-PositioningFrequencyLayer-r16 and NR-DL-PRS-Info-r16
Proposal 4:		The "index principle" as currently used for the NR-DL-PRS-AssistanceData is also used for the available on-demand DL-PRS configurations.
In the case of available on-demand DL-PRS configurations for multiple NR positioning methods are provided, the nr-On-Demand-DL-PRS-Configurations need to be present in only one of NR-Multi-RTT-ProvideAssistanceData, NR-DL-AoD-ProvideAssistanceData, or NR-DL-TDOA-ProvideAssistanceData. The applicable configuration is then defined as an index in these ProvideAssistanceData messages.
Proposal 7 (modified):	The previous agreement is modified as follows [see R2-2203620 for revmarked version]:
To respond to an unfulfilled UE-initiated on-demand PRS request, new location server error cause values are introduced indicating that on-demand DL-PRS assistance data are not available or not supported.
Proposal 8:	The value for maxDL-PRS-Configs-r17 is 8.

If the UE receives assistance data for a PRS-ID+cell ID combination for which it has already stored assistance data, it overwrites the stored assistance data.  If the UE receives assistance data for a PRS-ID+cell ID for which it has not stored assistance data, it maintains its stored assistance data for other PRS-ID+cell ID combinations.
UE capability for the number of PRS-ID+cell ID combinations for which the UE can store AD.

Proposal 6: RAN2 to agree new posSibType6-5  NR-DL-PRS-TRP-TEG-Info for the TRP Tx TEG info (10/11) and the TP of NR-DL-PRS-TRP-TEG-Info for broadcast(8/11) in the annex, FFS the description on resource association.
Proposal 8: RAN2 to agree the stage-3 design of RSTD measurements from different DL PRS resources per UE Rx TEG report in the annex (10/12).
Proposal 9 (modified): RAN2 to agree the updated stage-3 design of UE Rx-Tx time difference measurements obtained from different DL PRS resources per UE Rx TEG/ RxTx TEG in the annex (9/9), FFS the nr-UE-Tx-TEG-ID-r17 in case2 and case3 (pending RAN1).
DL-AoD enhancement
Proposal 14: RAN2 to agree the following option is taken on supporting LMF to provide the TRP beam/antenna information to UE: Option a: New IE to carry the TRP beam/antenna information, e.g., NR-TRP-BeamAntennaInfo in running CR of TS37.355. (8/12)
Proposal 16: As for the TRP beam/antenna information provided by the LMF to the UE for UE-based DL-AoD, RAN2 to agree that the peak power value that is used as the reference for other resource powers on a specific angle is not provided (12/12).
Proposal 17: RAN2 to agree that the value ranges of the relative power of DL-PRS resource should be decided by RAN1 (11/12).
Proposal 18: RAN2 to agree that keep RSRP still as mandatory within the measurement results info provided by UE to LMF for DL-AOD in R17 (10/12) ), and it may be revised if there is clear agreement from RAN1..
Proposal 19: RAN2 to agree that the value ranges of the RSRPP should be decided by RAN1 (11/12).
Proposal 20: RAN2 to agree that the angle assistance information (expected angel value and uncertainty) should be per TRP (12/12).
Proposal 21: RAN2 to agree to extend the R16 IE NR-DL-PRS-AssistanceDataPerTRP-r16 to carry the expected angle assistance information (like expected RSTD and expected RSTD uncertainty)(7/12), FFS with restrictions only applied for DL-AOD positioning method waiting for RAN1 feedback.
Proposal 22: RAN2 to agree that the value ranges of the expected angle assistance (expected angel value and uncertainty) relative power of DL-PRS resource should be decided by RAN1 (8/11).
Proposal 23: RAN2 to agree to extend the R16 IE NR-DL-PRS-Resource-r16 to carry the R17 DL-PRS resource priority list information, with restrictions that it is only applied for DL-AOD positioning method (8/12).
Proposal 24: RAN2 to agree that it is up to RAN1 to decide whether further description of UE behaviour needed related to the measurements and/or reporting is needed related to the prioritization of DL-AOD reporting.

Proposal 5: The UE may indicate its preferred on-demand PRS pre-defined configuration via a list in decreasing order of preference (i.e., sorted from the UE’s most preferred to least preferred on-demand PRS configuration). [10/14]
Proposal2 (modified): Differentiate the UE capability of time bases for different positioning modes. (7/12)
Proposal 2. The validity time of the integrity bounds is set as equal to the validity time of the SSR data. No additional validity time parameter is defined in Rel17.

Assistance information from the UE reader for additional resource allocation includes at least time domain and/or frequency domain information on quantity of resources needed.  For stage 3 discussion on the resolution/how many bits/etc.  This information is advisory for the gNB, i.e., up to network how/if to configure.
FFS if the assistance information includes something beyond the quantity of resources.

Burst information useful to report to scheduler (applicable for both 5G and 6G discussion)
Burst size of data already in the AS buffer
Burst size of current data in non-AS buffer (e.g. in the higher layer buffer already generated by not in AS buffer yet).
Burst size of expected data not yet in AS or non-AS buffer (i.e. it is not yet generated data).
Burst timing information can include expected time of first packet of burst available for transmission.  There is a desire to indicate to the network that data is there but in non-AS buffer due to being stuck, etc,.
FFS how this information is signalled to the network.
The above agreements from 6G session apply to R20 XR discussion as well

1	As in NR, there are two triggers for retransmission:
•	RLC retransmission to deal with data losses over the Uu
•	PDCP reestablishment, recovery
2	As in NR, retransmissions of both SDUs and SDU-segments are necessary.
3	A common L2 retransmission function is only possible with a single SN.  FFS details
For the next meeting, companies are encouraged to provide input on the following aspects:
•	Address the identified set of benefits and drawbacks of each approach to handle the two retransmission triggers
•	Single window operation when considering a CU-DU split (depending the RAN plenary decision on CU-DU split)
•	Common status reporting in case of different termination points for the two retransmission triggers

1	In addition to CFRA baseline for early UL synchronization in 6G mobility, RAN2 studies also the feasibility of UE using CBRA based early UL synchronization.  For CBRA-based the assumption is that the UE still is configured with a preamble to use for this purpose.
2	NW-triggered early UL synchronization is supported. Study further the potential benefits and feasibility of UE-triggered early UL synchronization
3	For NW-triggered early UL synchronization RAN2 considers the following steps to be a part of baseline procedure (FFS if any other enhancements are needed):
a.	Source cell initiates the procedure by transmitting a command to the UE
b.	UE transmits a RACH preamble to the indicated target cell
c.	Target cell is responsible to calculate the TA value and transmits it to the source cell
d.	Source cell is responsible to deliver the TA value to the UE
e.	With a valid TA value, UE performs a RACH-less mobility procedure
4	In mobility with pre-configuration, for network-triggered mobility, the resources for initial access to the target cell (e.g. CFRA, CG, SR): the following two cases are considered
-	Can be provided before cell switch command but be used upon cell switch command
-	Can be provided with cell switch command and be used.

A cluster can have one or multiple PF/PO
Support having gaps between Paging PF/PO within a cluster  (i.e., clustered paging)
Support configuration of multiple paging occasions associated with a paging frame
Support configuration of PO/PF close to common signals e.g. with SSB transmission
We aim to distribute UEs among Paging PO/PF
A RRC paging message should be able to address multiple UEs (e.g. like paging records in 5G).
Should be possible to have one or multiple paging clusters per UE paging DRX cycle.
From RAN2 point of view, paging mechanism in 6G allows network to:
Reach UEs in idle state and inactive state, through Paging messages.
Notify UEs at least in RRC Idle/Inactive states of system information change and ETWS/CMAS indications.  FFS whether SI change and ETWS/CMAS in RRC connected.
From RAN2 point of view, the paging capacity (including paging records) in 6G should be at least the same level as 5G.

Agreements for the study of C-DRX and WUS configured together
For the purpose of the discussion to find commonalities, we assume the following, but this doesn’t mean that WUS can be configured without DRX.  That will be studied separately.
For C-DRX we assume the following parametrs are needed (DRX cycle, Timer x( onDuration-like), and Timer y(inactivitytimer like))
For WUS we assume the following timer (WUS cycle, Timer x (PDCCH monitor timer), Timer y (inactivitytimer)
For the study of C-DRX and WUS configured - FFS UE behavior if WUS is not received and DRX is configured.  FFS if the cycles can same or different.  FFS if the timers x and y can be same or different.

Agreements on RRM measurement prediction
For UE-sided model, agreed to have only UE-sided performance monitoring (not to have NW-sided performance monitoring).
The RRM measurement and reporting framework can be adopted as a baseline for monitoring configuration and reporting of AI/ML mobility.
For UE sided monitoring network decision of temporal domain case A/B or inter-frequency prediction, a monitoring window is configured for the purpose of performance monitoring metric calculation.
Event-driven performance monitoring report, e.g. based on RSRP difference, is introduced. FFS on the need of periodic performance monitoring report.
For RRM measurement prediction, RSRP difference can be used as the performance metric for monitoring.
RAN2 have initial discussion on options and if possible, narrow-down options, and ask to RAN4.
RSPR difference is calculated based on the predicted instance and ground truth monitoring measurement result at the same or closest time points.
From RAN2 perspective, for temporal domain case A, the performance metric can be calculated to indicate: 1) Average RSRP difference among all predicted instances within the PW. FFS for MW. 2) RSRP difference of the last predicted instance within the PW. FFS for MW. Note 1: understand that the last one is assumed to be worst one. Note 2: other metrics can be further discussed, if justified.
From RAN2 perspective, for temporal domain case B, no need to consider PW when calculating the performance metric.
From RAN2 perspective, regarding multiple predicted cells, the following performance monitoring metric can be calculated to indicate: RSRP difference(s) for specific predicted cell(s) of the MO, FFS which cell(s). FFS whether we’ll have an average RSRP difference across the specific cells or a separate RSRP difference for each specific cell. Note: other metrics can be further discussed, if justified.
RAN2 confirms the following enhancement for input data report for NW-sided RRM measurement prediction. (Note that this does not exclude other potential enhancement for inference input for now.) 1) For inference input for RRM sub-case 2 of intra-frequency temporal domain Case A for L3 cell prediction, L3 cell-level RRM measurement results at multiple time instances can be included in one measurement report. 2) For inference input for RRM sub-case 5 of intra-frequency temporal domain Case A for L3 beam prediction, L3 beam-level RRM measurement results at multiple time instances per beam can be included in one measurement report.
For configuration of inference input reporting, reuse the existing IE (i.e., MeasObjectNR, MeasId, ReportConfigNR). For configuration of inference input reporting, introduce new fields to configure inference input reporting parameters in MeasObjectNR or ReportConfigNR IE if needed. For inference input report, reuse the existing message (i.e., MeasurementReport) and IE (i.e., MeasResultNR). For inference input report, introduce new fields to include inference input (e.g., L3 cell/beam-level RRM measurement results at multiple time instances) in MeasResultNR IE if needed. For inference input reporting, NW can configure both existing periodical and event-triggered reporting.
For NW-sided model, the UE can send time info together with the measurement results to the network. Absolute timestamp is not used for time info.
During RRC resume procedure, partial inference configuration in otherConfig is released.
For RRM measurement prediction, the associated ID is defined by directly reusing the R19 AI/ML PHY BM definition, i.e., (i) it is 24-bit long, (ii) its meaning is unique within a PLMN.
For inference condition for temporal domain Case A, any of A1 – A6 event can be used.
No special inference control is introduced and reuse the existing s‑Measure condition as the activation trigger for starting inference for inter‑frequency prediction.

Agreements for inactive state
1	Paging message is used to reach the UE for incoming DL data/signaling when the UE is in “inactive” state.  Same paging model as in idle is assumed.  How the paging signaling looks like is FFS (depending on RAN2/SA2/RAN1, etc discussions).
2	UE-based mobility in the “inactive” state should be the same as that in idle state, i.e. based on cell (re) selection framework (e.g., best cell principle, cell ranking, inter-freq/RAT prioritization, etc.), and can follow the progress of cell (re)selection made in mobility topic.
3	RRC based mechanism is used as baseline to perform the state transition from “inactive” state to RRC connected state from the UE.
4	Identify limitations/drawbacks/possible modification of 5G SDT, and understand the need for different use cases and traffic characteristics, the maximum TBS size.  Use 5G SDT analysis as a starting point and continue to understand the benefits/gains/limitation for such cases in terms of at least energy efficiency and signaling overhead, including mobility and coverage considerations.

Agreements on data collection
The following enhancements on NW side data collection in AI PHY can be reused for AI Mob. 1) Network-side data collection for Network-side model training can be initiated by OAM or by gNB. 2) Both periodic and L3 measurement event-triggered data logging are supported. 3) The UE stores the logged data at the AS buffer. When the AS buffer for storing logged data becomes full, the UE stops measurement and logging for data collection. When the AS buffer reserved for storing logged data becomes full or reaches an absolute threshold (if configured), the UE indicates data availability to the gNB. 4) When low power state is detected, the UE can indicate the low power state to the gNB. Upon reception of the low power state indication, the gNB should release the UE data collection configuration for Network-side model. NOTE: It is up to UE implementation how to determine the AS buffer threshold is reached and how to determine low power state. 5) The gNB can indicate UE whether the logged data should be kept or not during L3 handover. When indicated to keep the logged data, UE retains it during handover and indicates its availability after handover. 6) Upon receiving UEInformationRequest message from network, UE sends the logged data via UEInformationResponse message. 7) Upon transiting to RRC_IDLE or RRC_INACTIVE state UE releases logged data.
For AI-Mob, the UE can be configured to log the followings: 1) L3 cell level results, 2) L1 filtered beam level results. FFS whether we’re going to introduce new measurement quantity or it is configured by using appropriate k value. 3) L3 filtered beam results, 4) Cell identity information; for serving cell the cell identity information could be CGI if it is available or PCI + ARFCN otherwise. For neighboring cell, the cell identity is PCI+ARFCN. 5) Time information. Absolute timestamp is excluded in the option.
Following configuration framework is agreed: 1) measConfig is reused. 2) measurement object is reused. 3) FFS whether new logging configuration is introduced or legacy reporting configuration is used. Will be further discussed/decided in stage 3. 4) If logging configuration is introduced, logging configuraiton can be used to associate with the corresponding measurement object. If legacy reporting configuration is used, measID is used as legacy.
The logged data collection configuration for NW-side model training can configure at least the following information: 1) Associated measurement object info, 2) Measurement result type (e.g., L3 cell-level, L3 beam-level and/or L1-filtered beam-level measurement result, 3) Logging Periodicity, 4) Event-Triggered Logging Configuration
Logged AI mobility data shall be discarded upon RRC reestablishment, consistent with the Rel-19 AI/ML PHY agreement.
Confirm the agreements taken during the SI: 1) UE can request data collection configuration via UAI message. 2) The request can contain an indication on start or stop of data collection. 3) It is up to UE implementation when to send the request 4) The network can configure whether UE is allowed to initiate request.
Data collection related configuration(s) and associated ID(s) can be included in training data collection configuration.
Introduce UAI message for UE request of data collection measurement configuration. And it is up to UE implementation when to send the request. No prohibit timer is needed for UE indicating its preferred data collection configuration.
The following agreement was made: 1) If a preferred frequency is already configured by measurement object, UE can indicate MO id as preferred frequency 2) Else, UE can indicate the preferred frequency information. Restriction: For a given frequency or MO id, the UE is allowed to request once in a cell while the UE is in RRC connected.
The UE can send preferred list implying that it would like to start data collection on those configuration
The UE can send stop indication for all or a given data collection configuration.
For UE-side data collection, there is no need for the network to configure the contents of collected data.

A go-to-sleep indication is supported at least to stop ongoing R2D monitoring; when it is received, the device is allowed to stop monitoring for R2D MAC signalling.  FFS how long the device may sleep and whether it would apply also to paging monitoring.

To indicate a method which UE supports to determine HARQ-ACK codebook size, the UE signals the capability: codebook-HARQ-ACK-r13 (see:  TS36.331) as follows:
first bit of the capability set to "1" implies the UE supports the DAI-based codebook size determination
second bit is set to "1" if the UE supports the codebook determination based on the number of configured CCs.

To support Rel-13 CA aggregation enhancements, RAN1#82bis agreed (see: report):
eNodeB can configure by RRC signaling an eCA UE to determine HARQ-ACK codebook size according to either (a) or (b) as follows:
a) DAI based solution (…)
b) Number of configured CCs based solution (…)
Both solution (a) and solution (b) are mandatory feature as UE capability from RAN1 recommendation point of views for UEs supporting more than 5 CCs

The requirement added on codebook-HARQ-ACK-r13 in this specification, that was supposed to follow the recommendation, does not clearly reflect the RAN1 agreement:
“For both solutions, it is mandatory for UEs of this release of the specification if carrier aggregation with more than 5 DL component carriers is supported. “
source_rows.summary:
The following change is made:
codebook-HARQ-ACK-r13 capability is updated to reflect better RAN1#82bis agreement:
Both solution (a) and solution (b) are mandatory feature as UE capability from RAN1 recommendation point of views for UEs supporting more than 5 CCs

Impact analysis
Impacted functionality: This is a clarification related to UE capability

Inter-operability:
If the network is implemented according to the CR and the UE is not the UE may use single HARQ-ACK codebook size determination method that won’t allow more than 5 CCs configuration.
If the UE is implemented according to the CR and the network is not there is no interoperability issue.

source_rows.reason:
In dedicated MBMS cell, it should be possible to configure all subframes including subframe #0 and #5 as MBSFN subframe(s). However, (P)MCH cannot be scheduled in subframe #0 and #5. With the introduction of 3ms MBMS slot length (i.e., 0.37kHz subcarrier spacing) in Rel-16 (see R2-2001740), it is necessary that subframe #0 and #5 can be used for (P)MCH to improve network resource utilization.

For example, when allocating MBSFN subframes in four consecutive radio frames, the subframe#0 of the first radio frame can be non-MBSFN subframe and rest can be configured as MBSFN subframes using the existing configuration, i.e., using the following signaling in SIB1-MBMS.

NonMBSFN-SubframeConfig-r14 ::=			SEQUENCE {
radioFrameAllocationPeriod-r14		ENUMERATED {rf4, rf8, rf16, rf32, rf64, rf128, rf512},
radioFrameAllocationOffset-r14		INTEGER (0..7),
subframeAllocation-r14				BIT STRING (SIZE(9))
}

In addition, the bitmap sf-AllocInfo-r16 allows network to schedule the MCCH in any subframe (i.e., including subframes #0, #4, #5 and #9).

However, the existing signaling structure for MCCH transmission (i.e., using fourFrames and fourFrames-v1430) does not allow network to configure the subframe #0 and #5 in an MBSFN area reducing the MBMS throughput. In other words, subframes of (P)MCH as indicated by the field commonSF-Alloc do not include the MBSFN subframes #0 and #5.
MBSFN-SubframeConfig field descriptions
fourFrames
A bit-map indicating MBSFN subframe allocation in four consecutive radio frames, "1" denotes that the corresponding subframe is allocated for MBSFN. The bitmap is interpreted as follows:
FDD: Starting from the first radioframe and from the first/leftmost bit in the bitmap, the allocation applies to subframes #1, #2, #3, #6, #7, and #8 in the sequence of the four radio-frames.
TDD: Starting from the first radioframe and from the first/leftmost bit in the bitmap, the allocation applies to subframes #3, #4, #7, #8, and #9 in the sequence of the four radio-frames. The last four bits are not used. E-UTRAN allocates uplink subframes only if eimta-MainConfig is configured.
fourFrames-v1430
A bit-map indicating MBSFN subframe allocation in four consecutive radio frames, "1" denotes that the corresponding subframe is allocated for MBSFN. The bitmap is interpreted as follows:
FDD: Starting from the first radioframe and from the first/leftmost bit in the bitmap, the allocation applies to subframes #4 and #9 in the sequence of the four radio-frames.

When subcarrier spacing of 0.37kHz (i.e., MBMS slot length of 3 ms) is used, the throughput is reduced by 53.8% (i.e., only 6 MBMS slots out of 13 MBMS slots are usable for MCH) as shown in figure below.



Therefore, it is important that MBMS area configuration (i.e., MBSFNAreaConfiguration-r9) provided in MCCH channel can schedule the (P)MCH in subframe#0 and #5.
source_rows.summary:
Following changes are made.

The MBSFNAreaConfiguration-r9 is extended to include MBSFN-   SubframeConfig-v16xy to configure subframe #0 and #5 as MBSFN subframe.

Suffix in commonSF-Alloc-r14 is corrected as commonSF-Alloc-v1430 as this includes the configuration of additional subframes #4 and #9 without ignoring the configuration of commonSF-Alloc-r9, i.e., the field introduced in v1430 is a noncritical extension of r9 field.

Following clarification is added in the field description of commonSF-Alloc.
“If E-UTRAN includes commonSF-Alloc-v1430 and/or commonSF-Alloc-v16xy, it includes the same number of entries, and listed in the same order, as in commonSF-Alloc-r9.”

source_rows.reason:
The current RRC specification allows RLC out-of-order delivery configuration in any case.

However, the configuration of RLC out-of-order delivery enabling LTE PDCP out-of-order delivery (for the purpose of latency reduction) should not be allowed for normal AM and UM DRBs without t-Reordering since it can cause data loss and HFN desynchronization, which would be a very critical issue for AM and UM DRBs.

If the RLC entity of normal AM DRB and UM DRB without t-Reordering is configured with RLC out-of-order delivery, the associated PDCP entity will deliver out-of-order PDCP SDUs to upper layer without reordering latency but the data loss can happen due to fast PDCP receive window movement since LTE PDCP entity basically assumes in-order delivery from the RLC entity.
source_rows.summary:
To clarify that the PDCP entity uses t-Reordering if the associated RLC entity is configured with RLC out-of-order delivery to reduce latency.

Impact analysis
Impacted functionality:
PDCP t-Reordering

Inter-operability:
If the network is implemented according to the CR while the UE is not, the network assumes UE will use t-Reordeing but UE does not use it and thus the UE implementation may declare an error or the PDCP entity at UE side would deliver the out-of-order PDCP SDU to upper layer and the data loss and HFN desynchronization can happen.

If the UE is implemented according to the CR while the network is not, no inter-operability issues would be foreseen.

restored_rows.reason:
In dedicated MBMS cell, it should be possible to configure all subframes including subframe #0 and #5 as MBSFN subframe(s). However, (P)MCH cannot be scheduled in subframe #0 and #5. With the introduction of 3ms MBMS slot length (i.e., 0.37kHz subcarrier spacing) in Rel-16 (see R2-2001740), it is necessary that subframe #0 and #5 can be used for (P)MCH to improve network resource utilization.

For example, when allocating MBSFN subframes in four consecutive radio frames, the subframe#0 of the first radio frame can be non-MBSFN subframe and rest can be configured as MBSFN subframes using the existing configuration, i.e., using the following signaling in SIB1-MBMS.

NonMBSFN-SubframeConfig-r14 ::=			SEQUENCE {
radioFrameAllocationPeriod-r14		ENUMERATED {rf4, rf8, rf16, rf32, rf64, rf128, rf512},
radioFrameAllocationOffset-r14		INTEGER (0..7),
subframeAllocation-r14				BIT STRING (SIZE(9))
}

In addition, the bitmap sf-AllocInfo-r16 allows network to schedule the MCCH in any subframe (i.e., including subframes #0, #4, #5 and #9).

However, the existing signaling structure for MCCH transmission (i.e., using fourFrames and fourFrames-v1430) does not allow network to configure the subframe #0 and #5 in an MBSFN area reducing the MBMS throughput. In other words, subframes of (P)MCH as indicated by the field commonSF-Alloc do not include the MBSFN subframes #0 and #5.
MBSFN-SubframeConfig field descriptions
fourFrames
A bit-map indicating MBSFN subframe allocation in four consecutive radio frames, "1" denotes that the corresponding subframe is allocated for MBSFN. The bitmap is interpreted as follows:
FDD: Starting from the first radioframe and from the first/leftmost bit in the bitmap, the allocation applies to subframes #1, #2, #3, #6, #7, and #8 in the sequence of the four radio-frames.
TDD: Starting from the first radioframe and from the first/leftmost bit in the bitmap, the allocation applies to subframes #3, #4, #7, #8, and #9 in the sequence of the four radio-frames. The last four bits are not used. E-UTRAN allocates uplink subframes only if eimta-MainConfig is configured.
fourFrames-v1430
A bit-map indicating MBSFN subframe allocation in four consecutive radio frames, "1" denotes that the corresponding subframe is allocated for MBSFN. The bitmap is interpreted as follows:
FDD: Starting from the first radioframe and from the first/leftmost bit in the bitmap, the allocation applies to subframes #4 and #9 in the sequence of the four radio-frames.

When subcarrier spacing of 0.37kHz (i.e., MBMS slot length of 3 ms) is used, the throughput is reduced by 53.8% (i.e., only 6 MBMS slots out of 13 MBMS slots are usable for MCH) as shown in figure below.



Therefore, it is important that MBMS area configuration (i.e., MBSFNAreaConfiguration-r9) provided in MCCH channel can schedule the (P)MCH in subframe#0 and #5.
restored_rows.summary:
Following changes are made.

The MBSFNAreaConfiguration-r9 is extended to include MBSFN-   SubframeConfig-v16xy to configure subframe #0 and #5 as MBSFN subframe.

Suffix in commonSF-Alloc-r14 is corrected as commonSF-Alloc-v1430 as this includes the configuration of additional subframes #4 and #9 without ignoring the configuration of commonSF-Alloc-r9, i.e., the field introduced in v1430 is a noncritical extension of r9 field.

Following clarification is added in the field description of commonSF-Alloc.
“If E-UTRAN includes commonSF-Alloc-v1430 and/or commonSF-Alloc-v16xy, it includes the same number of entries, and listed in the same order, as in commonSF-Alloc-r9.”

restored_rows.reason:
The current RRC specification allows RLC out-of-order delivery configuration in any case.

However, the configuration of RLC out-of-order delivery enabling LTE PDCP out-of-order delivery (for the purpose of latency reduction) should not be allowed for normal AM and UM DRBs without t-Reordering since it can cause data loss and HFN desynchronization, which would be a very critical issue for AM and UM DRBs.

If the RLC entity of normal AM DRB and UM DRB without t-Reordering is configured with RLC out-of-order delivery, the associated PDCP entity will deliver out-of-order PDCP SDUs to upper layer without reordering latency but the data loss can happen due to fast PDCP receive window movement since LTE PDCP entity basically assumes in-order delivery from the RLC entity.
restored_rows.summary:
To clarify in PDCP-Config that the PDCP entity is configured with t-Reordering if the associated RLC entity is configured with RLC out-of-order delivery to reduce latency.

Impact analysis
Impacted functionality:
RLC out-of-order delivery, PDCP t-Reordering

Inter-operability:
If the network is implemented according to the CR while the UE is not, no interoperability problems are foreseen.
If the UE is implemented according to the CR while the network is not, the UE implementation may declare an error or the PDCP entity at UE side would deliver the out-of-order PDCP SDU to upper layer and the data loss and HFN desynchronization can happen.
